name: groundtron-combo
description: Four mods in one: savvy-progress (progress bar + /agents-info panel), filetree (IDE-style file tree, /filetree), cache-tax (/keepwarm, /cache-tax: keeps the prompt cache warm, guards cold sends; warming costs tokens) and blast-radius (holds risky Bash commands with Proceed/Cancel).

language.title: Agents panel: language
language.description: savvy-progress: auto follows Claude Code's language setting, then the system locale; en, ru or he (Hebrew, drawn right to left)

autoOpen.title: Agents panel: open on
autoOpen.description: savvy-progress: savvy = when a savvy-flow worker starts or a plan is reported; any = also when any other subagent starts

activity.title: File tree: Claude activity
activity.description: filetree: which of Claude's file activity shimmers in the tree: reads in purple, writes in orange, git actions in green

glyphs.title: File tree: glyphs
glyphs.description: filetree: auto uses Nerd Font icons when one is installed here, except in the desktop app; plain uses Unicode only

follow.title: File tree: follow Claude
follow.description: filetree: on = the tree scrolls to what Claude reads, writes or commits; off = the view stays where you put it

start.title: File tree: open at start
start.description: filetree: on = the pane opens when a session starts; off = it stays closed until you run /filetree

column.title: File tree: right column
column.description: filetree: date (last modified), age (time since last modified) or size

hints.title: File tree: hints
hints.description: filetree: on = outside a git repo, a line under the header says git status starts after git init

open.title: File tree: open with
open.description: filetree: what double-click or Enter does with a file. Empty = the default app; editor = $VISUAL/$EDITOR; preview = show it in the pane; anything else is a command, {path} the file and {dir} its folder

edit.title: File tree: edit with
edit.description: filetree: what e does in the preview. Empty = $VISUAL/$EDITOR; or a command where {line} is the line, e.g. code -g {path}:{line}
